RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.

1. WHICH BOUNDARY THE REPLAY COULD NOT CROSS, AND WHAT FWD-2's EXERCISED BAR STILL LACKS. Unchanged in KIND from IB-sb-3's own round-1 finding, and RE-CONFIRMED rather than assumed this turn: no mechanism exists for a worker to mint a valid RS256 JWT the portal-authorizer would accept (RT2_test_principal_human_gated.md's own investigation, re-checked verbatim, not re-derived -- the mint path is out of <paths>, a write to opal-users-v2, and the private-key alternative is forbidden by bound 6). What CHANGED since round 1: the population under test is now the FULL 12-route table (holdings added) and 6 of those routes (directory search/resolve, performance, ycharts-generate, narrative, export-render's three operations) moved from UNGUARDED/VACUOUS/STRUCTURALLY-EXEMPT to GUARDED between round 1 and round 2 (IB-rt-2's wrapper) -- so FWD-2's EXERCISED bar has grown from '5 of 11 routes reauthorization-testable' to '12 of 12 routes reauthorization-testable', all measured on the POST-AUTHORIZER plane. What STILL lacks: an authenticated six-swap run all the way through CloudFront -> edge validator -> API Gateway authorizer -> handler as one continuous real request, for any of the 12 routes. A second, narrower gap surfaced this turn and is distinct from the authentication gap: the download route's REAL-OBJECT grounding (arm c3a) cannot be exercised at all, because the only real synthetic PDF export objects the estate ever produced are now permanently gone (row W1-S18) -- so even a hypothetical authenticated replay of the download route would need a freshly-minted real artifact first.

2. WHICH ROUTE'S REFUSAL CAME FROM THE EDGE, THE AUTHORIZER AND THE HANDLER, AND WHETHER THAT LAYERING IS DESIGN-INTENDED. EDGE (CloudFront/auth-validator-edge): not independently isolated by this replay either, for the same reason as round 1 -- every real-path probe that reached the authorizer had already passed the edge Lambda. AUTHORIZER (opal-portal-authorizer, naqxlm): measured directly for all 12 routes this turn (was 11) -- the same three distinct refusal shapes as round 1 (missing/invalid header, malformed/forged JWT giving 'Invalid or expired token', and the CloudFront-bypass control giving API Gateway's own generic 'Unauthorized' when isOriginVerified() fails before JWT verification even starts) now hold across the FULL route set including holdings. HANDLER (via _authz.Enforcer.guard()): measured directly for all 12 routes now, not 5 -- FIRM_BINDING, OBJECT_NOT_COVERED, EMPTY_GRANT, UNPROJECTED_GRANT, CONTRACT_VERSION are all handler-layer codes, never edge or authorizer codes, and none appeared in a real-path probe (which never got past the authorizer). WHETHER THE LAYERING IS DESIGN-INTENDED: for all 12 routes now (was 5 of 11), three independent layers each refuse on a different question -- this reads as round 1's own open question (whether every route was meant to reach a handler-layer guard, or whether 6 of 11 simply had not been migrated yet) ANSWERED in the affirmative by round 2's own work: IB-rt-2's decomposition rectangle states explicitly that 'the unguarded three were protected by accident (a consent gate, an identity-less request shape, an absent operation)' and IB-rt-2 'replaces accident with the wrapper' -- so the design intent, as read from the issuer's own decomposition, was always a third layer everywhere, and round 1's gap was sequencing, not intent. This cell's own measurement is consistent with that reading (0 of 12 unguarded, with a working positive control) but cannot itself adjudicate intent versus sequencing -- that reading is the decomposition document's own words, cited rather than independently derived.

3. WHICH OF THE SIX GUARDS WAS EXERCISED ONLY IN-PROCESS. All six: firm, advisor, account, relationship, report and pdf. Every swap in arm (b) -- across all seven functions, both the six-function pytest run and holdings' own arm -- runs on the POST-AUTHORIZER plane (a real entry point invoked in-process with a fixture-substituted storage boundary), never through a live authenticated HTTP request. The REAL-PATH plane (arm a3) exercises none of the six guards at all -- it stops at the authorizer, before any of the six kinds of identity comparison a handler's guard() performs is ever reached. So the exercised bar for FWD-2 is: the AUTHORIZATION DECISION itself (all six guards, all twelve routes) is proven end-to-end against the real code, in-process; the CHANNEL that would carry a real authenticated request's claims into that decision (edge -> authorizer -> handler, in one request) is proven only up to the authorizer, and the handoff from a genuine JWT's claims into the header/context shape this cell assumed is not observed on a live request for any of the six guards.
